pick_photo: 🖼 What should I do with this photo?
pick_sticker: 🧩 What should I do with this sticker?
pick_video: 🎬 Make a GIF of this video?
pick_animation: 🎞 Turn this GIF into a video?
gone: This is no longer available — send the file again.
not_yours: Only the person who asked can use these buttons.
failed: ⚠️ That didn't work with this file.
too_big: This file is too big for me (photos up to 1280 px are used; files up to 20 MB).
limit: That's enough media tools for today.
off: Media tools are off in this group.
admins_only: Media tools are for admins in this group.
pack_added: 🧩 Your sticker is ready — it's also in your own pack.
pack_failed: I couldn't make the sticker: open a private chat with me first, then try again.
qr_long: That's too long for a QR code (up to 900 characters).
qr_none: I found no QR code I can read here. The Mini App can try with another method.
gif_added: 🎞 {n} photos for the GIF. Add more (up to 10), then make it.
gif_full: A GIF can have up to 10 photos.
ocr_open: 🔤 The text is read on your device (free, open-source Tesseract).
ocr_private: 🔤 Reading text works in a private chat with Aegis:
usage_rq: Reply to a photo with /readqr — or make one: /qr your text
usage_tl: Reply to a photo, sticker or video with /tools
pdf_not: This isn't a PDF I can read.
pdf_danger: 🚨 This PDF can run code or carry files — don't open it.
pdf_r_richmedia: It contains rich media (Flash or similar).
pdf_r_autoaction: It does something by itself when opened.
pdf_r_form: It has forms that send data.
pdf_r_remote: It opens other files or documents.
pdf_r_encrypted: It is encrypted — parts couldn't be checked.
pdf_r_obfuscated: Names in it are disguised (a trick to hide things).
pdf_note: Checked for known risky features; no check is perfect.
panel_intro: Members reply to media with /sticker, /tophoto, /gif, /qr, /readqr, /ocr, /pdf or /tools. Everything is made by Aegis itself, for free.
panel_security: Links in QR codes and PDFs that can run code are checked by Security → Suspicious content.
app_note: Everything is read here on your device with free, open-source libraries; the language data is downloaded once.
